summary: P0 admin auth stale-cookie fix VERIFIED end-to-end. Backend now prefers Authorization Bearer over the access_token cookie, so a stale non-admin cookie can no longer downgrade an admin request to 403. Backend pytest: 5/5 pass. Frontend: real admin login → /admin renders fully (Overview + Economy + Gameplay Tuning + Player Management + City Infrastructure + Underworld & Finance) with 0 admin 403s; stale-cookie UI scenario (player access_token cookie + admin Bearer in localStorage) also renders /admin cleanly with 0 admin 403s and no error toasts. Non-admin player is correctly redirected away from /admin. Cookie-only admin (no Bearer) still authenticates (fallback preserved).

test_player_bearer_with_stale_admin_cookie_is_still_403 → PASS (bearer precedence works in both directions)

critical_code_review_comments: backend/core.py current_user (line 81): fix looks correct and minimal — Authorization Bearer read first, cookie only used as fallback when no header token. Clear inline comment explains the intent. No security regression: token still validated via JWT + user lookup regardless of source.

OPTIONAL hardening (not blocking): consider clearing / re-scoping the access_token cookie on /auth/login for a different user, or namespacing the cookie name — this would prevent stale cookies from lingering across account switches on shared machines. Bearer-first fix already resolves the P0, but this would be defense-in-depth.

OPTIONAL: frontend /auth/logout could explicitly call a backend logout endpoint that clears the cookie (delete_cookie); currently only localStorage is cleared client-side so a stale cookie can persist in-browser.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The 403 Admin Dashboard bug from stale non-admin access_token cookie is FULLY FIXED and independently verified at both API and UI layers. Backend regression tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_admin_stale_cookie.py — keep running these on future auth/refactor work. Bearer-first precedence in current_user (backend/core.py:81) is the fix.
rca of the issue: Root cause: backend/core.py current_user previously read the httpOnly access_token cookie BEFORE the Authorization Bearer header. Because both /auth/login and /auth/register call set_auth_cookie(), whichever account last logged in on a given browser overwrote the cookie. The SPA sends withCredentials:true, so during account switches (e.g. QA logging out of a player and into admin, or vice versa via a different tab) the JWT resolved from the STALE cookie could belong to a non-admin user, causing admin_user() to raise 403 on /api/admin/*. Fix: current_user now reads Authorization: Bearer first (the SPA's active source of truth) and only falls back to the cookie when no header is present. Mitigation applied by main agent, verified by 5 pytest cases + 2 UI scenarios (real admin login, and stale-cookie override reproduction).
